newsitem.title: UK: London gold steady in lower, post-slump range.
newsitem.headline: London gold steady in lower, post-slump range.

text.p: The precious metals held to narrow trading ranges on Friday in a market uneasy after Thursday's slump in gold prices.
"It's not surprising that gold is pretty quiet today after yesterday's big move, a dealer said, pegging the near-term range at $375.50 to $377.50.
Bullion fixed virtually unchanged at $377.00 an ounce versus $376.90 in the morning and $377.00 on Thursday afternoon.
The fixings were lows since gold was set at $376.60 an ounce on March 6, 1995.
In New York's Comex futures market, December gold was $0.90 higher at $377.40 an ounce, after hitting a life-of-contract low of $375.80 on Thursday.
Prices had tumbled below a key technical support level around $377 an ounce on Thursday afternoon amid heavy selling pressure from speculators and producers and bearish sentiment.
"The selling was high quality, which is not to be bought back," one dealer said.
Physical demand from the Far East and light buying in Europe helped lift gold from Thursday's lows below $376 an ounce.
Initial price support was seen emerging at around $373, but eventually gold appeared destined to test still lower levels, said technical analysts watching historical price charts.
"There are willing sellers above the market. Gold is looking at an objective down to the $370 area," said analyst Cliff Green of Trend Analysis.
A period of consolidation within a lower price band and even small corrections higher were expected before prices sink to that key support level, Green added.
"But rallies are going to be shortlived and unsubstantial," he added.
Silver had slid some 10 cents on Thursday in sympathy with gold. It edged slightly higher in the afternoon and was indicated at $4.88/$4.90, up two cents from the London close.
But several dealers and analysts said it too was due to head down after its recent period of relative stability.
"Silver looks awful on the charts and it definitely has potential to slip lower towards the mid-$4.60," a dealer said, adding that some selling had entered the market.
Platinum was barely changed from Thursday's London close at $383.25/$384.25, and like silver still holding within its broader trading range of $380-$390.
